extracted.intended_audience: fiction writers (novelists and short-story authors) seeking satisfying endings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for evaluating and crafting the ending of a story or novel so it feels complete and emotionally/work-plot-wise earned. Focuses on pacing, closure, genre-appropriate resolution, treatment of fantastical elements, and character payoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Have you stopped in the right place?
rubrics_metrics.description: Are you cutting the story off before all main plot points are addressed, or are you dragging it out with unnecessary details? Strike a balance where the story feels complete, but not overly extended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance completeness and brevity: avoid ending too early (leaving key plot points unresolved) and avoid dragging the ending with unnecessary detail. Reflect on pacing — if the ending feels rushed it may indicate a broader pacing issue that needs revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Are you providing enough closure?
rubrics_metrics.description: Have you wrapped up every subplot and resolved every question, or have you left too many things open-ended? Aim for a satisfying amount of closure that aligns with the overall narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You don't have to answer every possible question in the reader's mind — provide enough payoff that readers feel the story has been properly paid off. The amount of closure should match the tone, length, and promises of the narrative; too many loose threads can feel unsatisfying, too much tying up can feel forced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is it the right kind of closure?
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider whether you've resolved the main conflict and provided an ending that satisfies readers given your genre and their expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Match closure type to genre and reader expectations. Types described:  
- Happy Ending: ends positively with goals achieved and contentment; satisfying for readers who want neat resolutions.  
- Tragic Ending: somber/devastating outcome, irreversible losses; evokes strong emotion and depth.  
- Ambiguous Ending: key elements open to interpretation; sparks reflection but risks frustrating readers if too many questions remain.  
- Circular Ending: mirrors the beginning to provide symmetry and reinforce themes and arcs.  
- Cliffhanger: abrupt with unresolved conflicts; useful for sequels or building anticipation.  
- Open-ended: leaves room for imagination but may provide more closure than a cliffhanger.  
- Conclusive Ending: ties up main plot and subplots, answers key questions for reader satisfaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Have you over-explained the supernatural or fantasy elements?
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the ending bogged down with explanations for the world's magic or fantasy features?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid heavy-handed exposition at the end. Let the story stand on its own without over-explaining fantastical mechanics; excessive explanation can sap mystery and slow the ending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Are you letting the supernatural or fantasy elements carry the ending too much?
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the world's magical or fantasy elements carrying the entire plot or resolution?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the ending is driven by character growth and narrative logic rather than solely by fantastical plot devices. Beware of Deus ex Machina solutions where magic or supernatural forces resolve conflicts in an unearned way; the ending should feel earned by character action and story cause-and-effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does the ending support the beginning, and vice versa?
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there a cohesive link between the start and end of your story? Ensure the ending supports the story's beginning, and that the beginning supports the ending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for cohesion between opening and closing (not necessarily identical). This can be achieved via thematic echoes, mirrored imagery, or narrative inevitability; the goal is to provide a sense of completion that feels consistent with how the story started.

rubrics_metrics.name: Have your characters worked hard enough for this ending?
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the challenges your characters face believable and rewarding? Make sure the ending reflects realistic struggles, allowing characters to earn their victory or learn from their losses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The payoff must feel hard-won: characters should have faced credible obstacles and undergone believable change. If the ending negates or short-circuits the struggles characters endured, it will feel unearned and unsatisfying.
